en: "...That's the situation, but I'm ashamed to admit that unless it's something healing or Dispel works on, I'm just hopeless at dealing with it......"{w}{p}"If it's not too much trouble, could you go chase them off for me?"{w}
note: 'them' = the stray dogs desecrating the nameless cemetery (slice_07 row 558). 'healing or Dispel works on' = undead; Dispel is the class ability name (JOB_EX [JP]).

en: "As for your reward: flawless after-sales service! That's my offer.{w}
note: [JP] kept as 'after-sales service' (sales-pitch joke for a money-grubbing priest; echoes slice_07 row 559 [JP] -- align that row). Rows 561/562/563 share this sentence word-for-word because 562 re-displays 561 inside {0E}..{0F} and 563 is a variant of the same line.

en:
{0E}"As for your reward: flawless after-sales service! That's my offer.{0F}
I'm counting on you, all right?"{w}{p}"I can't let this temple's reputation take a hit."{w}{p}"Oh, and please keep this matter between us.{w}...I am 'Hardy the Money-Grubber,' after all."{w}
note: 'Hardy the Money-Grubber' as in pilot row 342.

en:
"As for your reward: flawless after-sales service! That's my offer.
I'm counting on you, all right?"{w}{p}"If the dead can't even rest in peace... this temple's good name will be tarnished."{w}
"Come right in, welcome to Rust Tem...{w}

{0E}"Come right in, welcome to Rust Tem...{0F}
Oh! It's you!{w}Thank you so much!"{w}
"...By the way, are any of you hurt?"{w}
"No, no, you've truly saved me.{w}If I can't even look after the place where they sleep, it would affect the number of corpse-- er, customers brought in to us."{w}
note: Source: Hardy almost says 'corpses' ([JP]) and corrects to 'customers'; kept the slip.

en: "...Let me see... Money is important.{w}There's a surprising amount you can do with money, you know.{w}A warm meal, a bed where you won't freeze... things like that."{w}

"But you could also say we're prisoners of money.{w}So at the very least, once people die, whatever their money,{w}I'd like them to rest in peace... That's what I believe."{w}{p}"...That wasn't like me at all, was it?
Please forget I said it."{w}
note: 'prisoners of money': subject unstated in source; rendered as general 'we' (people in general), which the next sentence about the dead supports.

en:
"Now then... about your reward...
I've given it a lot of thought since then."{w}

"The truth is... the other day, even though it's a nameless cemetery, a bereaved family came to visit -- who knows how they tracked it down.{w}And, well... they actually thanked me..."{w}{p}"Then they donated a huge supply of medicine the deceased had left behind... Combined with our own stockpile, there's no way we could ever use it all."{w}{p}"So last night, I quietly dropped it all off at Kembeck's Shop.{w}
note: 'a bereaved family': the family of someone buried there; number/gender unspecified, kept as 'a bereaved family'.

en:
{0E}"So last night, I quietly dropped it all off at Kembeck's Shop.{0F}
...I do have a reputation as a money-grubber to keep up, after all."{w}
note: Joke: he did it secretly because a known miser can't be seen giving things away.

en: "I'm sure it's lined up on the shelves by now.{w}Please, make good use of it.{w}Think of it as an advance on that reward."{w}

note: Item names are proposals (ITEM.CSV 420/415/416, 16-char limit, not yet translated): [JP] Full Heal Potion (full HP), [JP] Paralysis Cure, [JP] Nightdew Lozenge (cures Silence). Must be synced with the ITEM.CSV translation. Here {0E}..{0F} wraps a fresh notice, not a re-display.

Proposed item names (ITEM.CSV 417/418/419): [JP] Calming Herb (cures Confusion), [JP] First Love Gem (cures Charm; 'First Love Flower Crystal' is 25 chars, over the 16-char item limit), [JP] Stone-Cure Water (cures Stone). Sync with ITEM.CSV.
The party's answer (nobody dead) happens between pages; 'Did I say something odd?' reacts to the party's look at a bishop being glad of no business.

en: You offered a silent prayer.{w}
Strange Bookmarks tucked into your adventure: {0B:0003:0057}.{w}{p}It seems that by praying, you could remove one of them.{w}
note: [JP] = 'Strange Bookmark' (ITEM_PRIZ.CSV:20 name, max 18). Sentence rebuilt as 'X: {n}' so it reads correctly for any count, including 1.

en: Remove one Strange Bookmark?
Who will pay?
Not enough money.{w}
note: dupes=6: kept as a generic system line without a subject so it fits every payer/shop.

en: "You wish to perform the Rite of Flux?"{w}{p}"......{w}My predecessor told me that rite is not something to be done lightly."{w}{p}"If you truly insist, I will perform it, but......"{w}
note: [JP] = 'Rite of Flux' (new term; also HELP_TEXT 256/284/285 menu label).

en: The Rite of Flux is a ritual that randomly relocates valuable items you have not yet obtained.{w}{p}This cannot be undone, so please be careful.{w}
note: Source literally 'the current state cannot be restored' -> 'this cannot be undone'.

en: Perform the Rite of Flux?
"Just to be sure, I have to ask..."{w}
"You truly wish to perform the Rite of Flux?"
note: data row is the yes/no prompt question, not a choice; 45 chars. Short form if needed: '"Truly perform the Rite of Flux?"'.

en: "Very well.{w}The cost will be an offering of 100,000 GP."{w}
note: [JP] written 'GP' as in pilot row 281.

en: Will you pay?
"Then let us begin the rite."{w}
The valuables you have not yet obtained scattered once more to places throughout the world.{w}
"May this rite bring light to the road that lies before you all..."{w}
"Everyone, it seems your offering is... a little short."{w}
"I see. That may well be a wise decision.{w}Trials are not something to avoid, but something to face."{w}{p}"May the blessings of Ildraha be with you all..."{w}
note: Blessing phrased as in pilot row 372.

en: "Then I can't perform the rite..."{w}
The castle is silent.{w}If you linger here any longer, you'll be taken for intruders.{w}It would be better to come back during the day.{w}
When you told the guards you had come about the Proclamation, they showed you to the audience chamber.{w}
note: Source literally 'had seen the Proclamation and come' -> 'had come about the Proclamation'.

en: The audience chamber is already crowded with adventurers.{w}The girls you saw at the inn earlier seem to be here too.{w}
note: [JP] 'girls' is the source's own word (Electra and company from the inn scene, pilot rows 240-285).

en: "Hello.{w}Sorry you had to see that embarrassing scene earlier.{w}I'm Electra. Nice to meet you."{w}
note: 'that embarrassing scene earlier' = the stable squabble with Mig at Zeppo's Inn (pilot rows 241-285).

en:
"They treat me like a horse here too!
Algrantz is a rude city full of rude people!"{w}
"Oh, let it go already.{w}...I wonder if unicorns are rare?{w}Everyone treats Mig like a horse."{w}
note: First sentence is to Mig, then Electra muses to the party; 'Mig' named instead of a pronoun (gender unknown).

en:
While you were chatting, the entrance doors opened.
You heard the guards snap to attention.{w}Soon, one of the guards came up right in front of you.{w}
Guard

"King Balgert will arrive shortly!"{w}{p}"We are also joined, from the Star Capital Lumisthenes, by the fortune-teller Natori and by Mayleen of the Stargazing Lighthouse!"{w}{p}"All of you, mind your manners!
No idle chatter!"{w}
note: [JP] on Natori/Mayleen not rendered as Lady/Lord (genders unknown in glossary); the guard's formal register carries the respect. [JP] = 'Stargazing Lighthouse' (new term).

en: Then, with a ringing of steel, the king appeared, clad in golden armor.{w}
The fortune-tellers followed.{w}
The two at the back don't seem to be from this city.{w}Amid the murmuring around you, you can make out the word 'Lumisthenes.'{w}
"What? This is all that showed up?"{w}
"Fewer and fewer come each time, it seems."{w}
note: 'each time': the Proclamation summons has been held repeatedly (pilot row 170 'again').

en:
"Can't be helped...{w}Waitin' around ain't gonna bring in any more,
so let's just get this started."{w}
note: Balgert's rough [JP] speech rendered with light dropped g's / ain't; keep consistent in later Balgert rows.

en:
"The name's Balgert.
I'm king of this here fortress city, Algrantz."{w}{p}"...Look at you, all scruffy and grubby.{w}Just like me when I was young! Hahaha!"{w}{p}"I called you all here for one reason and one reason only.{w}To help take back the Palace of the Sun!"{w}{p}"Now, the Palace of the Sun, see...{w}

{0E}"Now, the Palace of the Sun, see...{0F}
It's... uh... that thing...{w}It's all shiny and glowin'... and it's a palace..."{w}{p}"Basically, it's huge... and real tall...{w}

{0E}"Basically, it's huge... and real tall...{0F}
Natori! You explain it to 'em!"{w}
"Huh? Oh, right, right."{w}
"Hi, everyone, nice to meet you!"{w}{p}"I'm Natori, from the Temple of Rafa in Lumisthenes. Let's get along!{w}And this grumpy-looking one here is Ms. Mayleen!"{w}
note: [JP] = 'Temple of Rafa' (pilot row 1). [JP] is the source's own honorific for a (learned) woman, rendered 'Ms.'; flag for glossary gender of Mayleen (still 'unknown' there).

en: "......{w}Enough of this nonsense. Get to the point, would you?"{w}
"Aww, what? I was trying to liven things up...{w}...Tch."{w}
"Ahem. Well then, let's start over."{w}
"I'm going to give you all a quick rundown of the crisis we're facing right now."{w}

"Since ancient times, this land has prospered under the light of the Palace of the Sun, high up in the heavens."{w}{p}"The sun god Rafa dwells in the Palace of the Sun, shining a purifying light that protects this land from the Kin of Darkness."{w}{p}"We people of Lumisthenes have prayed every single day, keeping watch over how Rafa is faring. But, you see..."{w}{p}"That Palace of the Sun has now fallen into the hands of the Kin of Darkness."{w}
note: [JP] = 'the Dark Kin' (new term; 83 occurrences corpus-wide, needs a glossary entry). [JP] rendered plain 'Rafa' (no Lord/Lady: gender unknown). 'keeping watch over how Rafa is faring' = literally inquiring after Rafa's condition.

en:
"With the Palace of the Sun in the hands of the Kin of Darkness, all sorts of effects are starting to show across the land."{w}{p}"The purifying light has gone murky, and the power that protects the land is fading away."{w}{p}"Lately the Kin of Darkness have been showing up more often and getting more vicious than usual,
and that's probably why."{w}

"Recently, we sent envoys to the rulers of every land to inform them of the situation at the Palace of the Sun, and received several proposals for breaking the deadlock."{w}{p}"From King Balgert of Algrantz, we received a proposal to revive the legendary 'Stairway of Light' and storm the Palace of the Sun."{w}{p}"The Stairway of Light is..."{w}
note: [JP] = 'Stairway of Light' (new term). [JP] -> 'rulers of every land' (neutral).

en:
"How about that!
Pretty good idea, don'tcha think!?"{w}{p}"The legendary Palace of the Sun, reached by the legendary Stairway of Light!{w}Go on, Mayleen, keep it goin'!!"{w}
"......I shall continue."{w}

"The Stairway of Light is the stairway Rafa is said to have used when ascending to the Palace of the Sun."{w}{p}"We were aware of the legend that it lies in Konnu, but its existence has yet to be confirmed."{w}
note: [JP] = 'Konnu' (new name; dungeon [JP] = Konnu Grassland Ruins in DGN_NAME). Subject of 'were aware' (unstated) taken as 'we' (Lumisthenes), matching row 622's 'we sent envoys'.

en: "So that's why you've all been called here.{w}We in Lumisthenes will cooperate in every way we can to get this situation under control, too."{w}
"We will now hand out compasses for finding the site where the Stairway of Light once stood -- in other words, the 'Lightstair Ruins.'"{w}
note: [JP]: coined word with a reading gloss; the gloss is dropped in English. 'Lightstair Ruins' (16 chars) chosen to fit ITEM_PRIZ.CSV:4 compass-target name (max 18) -- the camp menu label must use the same string (rows 635 and slice_09+).

en: "Normally, you'd have to come to Lumisthenes for us to give a compass its power, you know?"{w}{p}"But today, we've prepared them specially.{w}So take one home with you!"{w}
A compass was placed in each of your hands.{w}
"Hahaha!!{w}You lot, this compass is somethin' else, y'know!?"{w}{p}"This compass, see...{w}

{0E}"This compass, see...{0F}
The compass... it's... uh... that thing...{w}
"Why, I have been explaining it all along, have I not?"{w}
note: Mayleen already explained the compass (row 627); dry put-down.

en: "Uh, r-right..."{w}

"Now then, everyone.{w}I will say this only once, so listen carefully."{w}{p}"Once you enter the ruins at Konnu, the first thing to do is set up camp."{w}{p}"In camp, be sure to set your compass's search target to the 'Lightstair Ruins.'"{w}{p}"If there are any clues nearby, the light should point you to where they are."{w}

"The light changes color depending on how far you are from what you're looking for."{w}{p}"Red means you're in the wrong place entirely.{w}Blue means it's the right place but the wrong floor.{w}Yellow means it's right nearby!"{w}
"You can turn off the compass's light by setting the search target to 'None.'{w}Feel free to turn it off whenever you don't need it."{w}
note: 'None' ([JP]) must match the camp compass menu label once the UI is translated.

en:
"And that's the briefing!
Don't worry, with this many people we'll manage somehow.{w}Good luck!!"{w}
"There is one more item being issued.{w}That would be this: the Angel's Window.{w}A handy device that shows you your surroundings."{w}
note: [JP] = 'Angel's Window' (proposed item name, ITEM.CSV 460, max 16; automap gem).
